items.title: Petitions
notes: A petition from Fightback KW was received for information.

items.title: Kelly Smith, FRIENDS of Waterloo Region Museums
notes: K. Smith appeared before Council on behalf of the FRIENDS of Waterloo Region Museums. She provided an overview of the fundraising work that the organization has undertaken, noting that they have donated almost $500,000 since 1998 to enhance programing at Regional museums. She noted that in 2024 they expanded their mandate to include fundraising support for Schneider Haus and McDougall Cottage, which unites all four Regional sites into their activities. She announced that they are providing 3 donations totaling over $100,000 over the next 3 years.

items.title: Wren Wombwell, Organizer, Fightback KW with Andrew Reeves, Jaime Stief and Acer Bonaparte
notes: A. Reeves spoke in support of the petition from Fightback KW. He noted that in the last 12 years there has been a significant decline in renting opportunities and that, given the magnitude of the housing crisis, the demands in the petition are reasonable. A. Reeves outlined the demands in the petition including freezing the Waterloo Region Police Services budget for 5 years, halting construction at 100 Victoria Street until there are housing solutions for all current and future residents, and a meaningful review and overhaul of the shelter system.

items.title: Krista Straus, Wilmot
notes: K. Straus appeared in opposition to the land assembly in Wilmot Township, noting that it is causing uncertainty in the farming community, which would not be done to any other industry. She stressed that agriculture is a vital industry in Wilmot Township and many other businesses depend on this sector. K. Straus highlighted the lack of public consultation on the project and stated that the residents support farmers and want the Region to look for sites closer to the Cities.

items.title: Stewart Snyder, Wilmot
notes:
S. Snyder appeared before Council in opposition to the land assembly in Wilmot Township, noting that land owners and residents have assembled in opposition to the land assembly. He expressed concerns with the lack of communication from the Region, the unknown final use of the land, and how water quality and transportation will be affected.

In response to a question from Council, S. Snyder stated that Vive Development knew enough about the project to assume that they were aware of the Region’s plans in advance.

items.title: Planning and Works Summary - May 7, 2024
notes: Responding to questions, Jennifer Rose, Commissioner, Engineering & Environmental Services, stated that staff can arrange for the new waste bins to be brought in for Council to see, but that they are an industry standard. She further noted that the costs of the new bins will be a capital cost for the Region and that the new automated system addresses issues of staffing and safety. The ongoing waste collection study for downtown’s will address collection in those areas.

items.title: Community and Health Services Summary - May 7, 2024
Board of Health Update
notes:
Dr. Hsiu-Li Wang, Commissioner, Public Health & Paramedic Services/Medical Officer of Health provided an update noting that 119 secondary students were suspended for out of date vaccination records, but since November over 37,000 immunization records have been updated. She highlighted that there has not been a report of a local case of measles yet, but Public Health is prepared to respond. Dr. H. Wang stressed that as a direct result of enforcement of the Immunization of School Pupils Act the Region’s compliance rate for measles vaccinations is approximately 95.8%.

Received for information.

items.title: Councillor C. James Notice of Motion
notes:
C. James introduced the motion noting that the current name of the Planning and Works Committee is not reflective of the work that comes before the Committee and the revised name will better help the community understand what the committee does.

In response to a question from Council, William Short, Regional Clerk, stated that in order to put the name change into effect, an amendment to the Procedure By-law is necessary, so the earliest the change can be made is for the August Committee meeting.

items.title: Questions
notes:
N. Salonen asked if staff could provide information regarding the hydro cut parking on Snyders Road, and noted that the Mennonite relief sale will be on Saturday and requested that the grass be cut on the road into New Hamburg.

S. Foxton requested that during the Trussler Road and Cedar Creek Road roundabout construction that no truck signs be placed on Trussler Road and Northumberland Street to prevent trucks from traveling on Piper Street. J. Rose stated that staff can work with Township staff on the issue.

J. Liggett noted that she has received a request from a business that the paving of the roundabout at Beverly and Dundas Streets be moved from Saturdays to a less busy day. J. Rose stated that staff will look into what can be done, but noted that there is only one day where paving will occur in front of the plaza.

D. McCabe requested that staff look at light crossing times as a part of the integrated mobility planning process. Doug Spooner, Acting Commissioner, Transportation, stated that staff can provide an update.

C. James requested information related to the Freeport bridge. J. Rose noted that the bridge is currently under load restrictions and staff can provide information on the construction timing.

In response to a question from D. McCabe, R. Regier stated that information was circulated to Council in response to questions about the delegation of planning authority to area municipalities, but noted it can be re-sent.

Responding to a question from D. Craig, M. Goetzke and D. Spooner stated that considerations for a pedestrian bridge across the Grand River at Galt Collegiate and River Bluffs Park need to be a part of the integrated mobility plan which will be put out to tender shortly and that bridge can be put into the scope.

motions.item_title: Councillor C. James Notice of Motion
motions.text: WHEREAS the title of Planning and Works no longer represents the full scale of the committee's responsibilities and can be confusing to residents; AND WHEREAS the Region’s strategic priority “Climate Aligned Growth”, our climate goals, our commitment to our natural heritage system, including rivers and streams, water and ground water resources, transit, waste and other environmental issues could be better represented by "Sustainability” AND WHEREAS the title should be modernized from the non-descriptive term "Works" to the more descriptive term "Infrastructure " including roads, transportation, waste, water and wastewater facilities; AND WHEREAS the Region’s strategic priority “Housing for All” directs our commitment to land readiness and the more accurate term “development” to support both housing and employment solutions for the Region’s growing population; THEREFORE be it resolved that the title of the standing committee Planning and Works be updated to the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Standing Committee.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the title of Planning and Works no longer represents the full scale of the committee's responsibilities and can be confusing to residents;
AND WHEREAS the Region’s strategic priority “Climate Aligned Growth”, our climate goals, our commitment to our natural heritage system, including rivers and streams, water and ground water resources, transit, waste and other environmental issues could be better represented by "Sustainability”
AND WHEREAS the title should be modernized from the non-descriptive term "Works" to the more descriptive term "Infrastructure " including roads, transportation, waste, water and wastewater facilities;
AND WHEREAS the Region’s strategic priority “Housing for All” directs our commitment to land readiness and the more accurate term “development” to support both housing and employment solutions for the Region’s growing population;
THEREFORE be it resolved that the title of the standing committee Planning and Works be updated to the Sustainability, Infrastructure and Development Standing Committee.
